title: Verbs: words for doing and being
examples: Does every sentence need a verb?

explain.say: Jump up, then sit down! Jump and sit are verbs, words that tell you what someone does. Look at the first box on the board: run, jump, eat, write, dance. Can you act one of them out?

draw.text: Verbs: words for doing and being

explain.say: Some verbs show no action at all. See the second box: am, is, are, was, were. These are being verbs. In I am nine, am joins you to being nine. Can you make a sentence with is?
Verbs can change their ending to tell you when. Look at the board: jump plus ing makes jumping, so it is happening right now. What are you doing now? I am reading!
Now swap the ending to ed: jumped. See ed glowing? It means it already happened, in the past. Yesterday I jumped in a puddle. Can you change play into the past?

Amazing! Look back at the doing box. Every full sentence needs a verb. Wow fact: Go! is a whole sentence, just one verb, because everyone knows it means you go. Challenge: find the verb in Ana kicks the ball.

faq.a: A verb is a word for an action or a state of being, like run, eat, is or was. It tells you what happens in a sentence.
Yes. Is, am, are, was and were are forms of the verb be. They are being verbs, not action verbs.

faq.q: Does every sentence need a verb?
faq.a: Yes, a full sentence needs at least one verb. Without one, like The big red bus, it is only a phrase.
asks: Can a sentence have no verb?

faq.a: Verbs change their ending or add a helper word: I jump now, I jumped yesterday, I will jump tomorrow.
asks: How do verbs change for past?

faq.q: What is the shortest sentence in English?
faq.a: Go! is a full sentence. The person doing it, you, is understood, so the verb can stand alone.
asks: Can one word be a sentence?

facts: Go! is a complete English sentence: the subject you is understood.
Be is the most irregular English verb, with the forms am, is, are, was, were, been and being.

quiz.say: Which word is the verb? Kofi sings in the choir.
quiz.show: Which word is the verb? Kofi sings in the choir.
quiz.why: Sings is what Kofi does, so it is the verb.

wrong.0: Kofi is a noun, the person doing the action.
wrong.2: choir is a noun, a group of singers.

quiz.say: Which ending shows a verb happened in the past?
quiz.show: Which ending shows a verb happened in the past?
quiz.why: Jumped, played and wanted all end in ed for the past.

wrong.0: ing shows it is happening now.
wrong.1: ly makes an adverb, like slowly.
